summary: The decomposition is largely coherent, boundary-safe, and organized around usable workflow slices, but it does not yet assign every v1 requirement to an implementing task. Task 010 currently masks several omissions as a horizontal catch-all. Correct the delivery-workspace, metadata-policy, status/locking, and topology-ordering gaps before creating issues.

blockingFindings.finding: FR-007 is only partially covered. Task 002 creates a delivery ID and ledger entry but no task owns creating the feature branch in a linked worktree or preventing product work directly on authoritative main. Tasks 003, 006, and 007 assume that workspace already exists.
blockingFindings.recommendation: Extend task 002 into the complete delivery-workspace slice: atomically establish the delivery ID, feature branch, linked worktree, and ledger entry; reject work on main; and add disposable-Git coverage for creation, resume, ambiguity, and cleanup handoff.

blockingFindings.finding: FR-008 requires unclassified or conflicting path ownership to block synchronization, promotion, and finalization. Task 001 validates path-policy schemas, while task 006 appears to implement classification later; task 004 has no metadata-policy guard, and tasks 006/007 do not explicitly revalidate it during finalization.
blockingFindings.recommendation: Place the shared one-owner path-classification engine in task 001 or another prerequisite available to task 004. Require task 004 to apply it before sync and tasks 006/007 to revalidate it before promotion/certification and finalization.

blockingFindings.finding: No task explicitly owns the complete FR-018 status projection: delivery phase, product/ledger/destination SHAs, acceptance freshness, PR states, locks, graph freshness, blockers, and next safe command. Task 001 also claims AC-021 without an acceptance criterion implementing mutation locking. Relying on task 010 to close all ACs makes it a horizontal implementation catch-all rather than a release-verification gate.
blockingFindings.recommendation: Define the status model and lock primitive in task 001, require each subsequent slice to contribute its status fields and use repository mutation locks, and assign final public-status integration to task 008 or explicit contributing criteria. Keep task 010 focused on fault injection and release-wide verification.

blockingFindings.finding: Tasks 006 and 007 are mutually conflicting but have no deterministic dependency order, even though task 007 says it will reuse shared promotion manifests and resolve the task-006 dispatcher conflict. A scheduler can legally select task 007 first.
blockingFindings.recommendation: Either make task 007 depend on task 006 and remove the ambiguous conflict, or move the shared topology dispatcher/manifests into an earlier prerequisite so 006 and 007 become genuinely independent parallel slices.

nonBlockingSuggestions.suggestion: Clarify how provider mutation checkpoints are persisted while tasks 002 and 003 run in parallel—task 003 can own idempotent provider discovery, but a named later integration criterion should bind provider IDs and resume state into the ledger.

Its dependency on task 003 is conservative; if acceptance and independent Codex review can operate entirely from Git and ledger state, consider depending only on task 002 and integrating development-PR presentation afterward.

The staged-pair task is a large but legitimate vertical slice. Add internal milestones for initial promotion, append-only revision, and post-merge finalization so its 40–52 hour scope remains reviewable without splitting the end-to-end contract.
State explicitly that CCPM is used only through the supported Codex path in v1; Claude Code and Cursor execution remain documentation-only deferred integrations.

dependencyAssessment: The graph is acyclic and exposes useful parallelism: tasks 002 and 003 after 001; task 004 after provider authority; task 005 after ledger/provider foundations; and task 009 alongside the core delivery work. Task 008 already receives task 004 transitively through task 006, and task 010 correctly waits for every functional slice. The material defect is the unordered 006/007 conflict despite task 007 expecting shared artifacts from task 006. Checkpoint integration between 002 and 003 should also be made explicit.
issueSyncAssessment: The records authorize CCPM epic/task issue creation only in visualjc/agentic-shipyard and explicitly prohibit internal workflow issues in NativeInteractive/agentic-shipyard. They are safe to synchronize only if bootstrap uses the D-004 guarded path: an explicit visualjc/agentic-shipyard target, command-scoped visualjc credential with verified API identity, and no raw CCPM command that infers the repository from origin. No Claude, Cursor, JustGames, repository-provisioning, predecessor-migration, or destination-issue work is authorized by these tasks.
